text: Every trigger and every action in Flow Designer produces output, and Flow Designer exposes that output as data pills — small draggable tokens you drag straight into a later step's input field. There's no scripting involved, and no typing field names by hand; you simply drag the pill where you need it.

Say your flow triggers on Incident Created. The trigger immediately exposes pills for every field on that incident — Short Description, Priority, Caller, and more. Drag the Short Description pill into a Notify action's message body, and at runtime Flow Designer swaps that pill for the real value from the record that actually fired the flow.

A flow variable is a genuinely different idea. It's a value you explicitly define up front, in the Flow Variables panel on the flow's properties, completely independent of any trigger or step output. You give it a name, a data type, and optionally a default value — then it behaves like a pill you can drag into any field, anywhere in the flow.

So how do you choose? Use a data pill whenever the value already exists upstream — on the trigger record or in a prior step's output. Use a flow variable for constants, calculated values, or anything reused across steps that has no natural upstream source to pull from in the first place.

Picture a flow with a flow variable holding an approval threshold of one thousand dollars, compared directly against a data pill carrying the requested item's actual price pulled from a Look Up Record action. One value was defined by the flow designer; the other came straight from the record — yet both get referenced the exact same drag-and-drop way.

Data pills move real record data between steps. Flow variables hold the constants and working values the logic itself depends on. Most real flows end up using both side by side. Next up: branching that logic into two different paths with If/Else conditions.
